questions.question: Which situation is best modeled by a combination?
options: Choosing $4$ students for four distinct roles
Drawing $4$ names with replacement, order ignored
Choosing $4$ students for an unordered group
Choosing $4$ students and lining them up

questions.question: Why is a committee without roles a combination rather than a permutation?
options: Changing the order of the listed members does not change the committee
No member can be chosen twice, so repeated choices never occur
The committee is smaller than the group it is drawn from
Members are picked one after another, so the order of picking is recorded

questions.question: Why is $\binom nk$ smaller than $n!/(n-k)!$ when $1<k<n$?
options: The combination count allows repeated elements
The permutation count distinguishes the $k!$ orders of each chosen group
The permutation count ignores order while the combination count records it
The two counts are always equal for finite sets

questions.question: Let $A$ be a set with $n$ elements and let $0\le k\le n$. Which object is a $k$-combination of $A$?
options: An ordered list of $k$ distinct elements of $A$
A subset of $A$ with exactly $k$ elements
An ordered list of $k$ elements of $A$, repeats allowed
An unordered collection of $k$ elements of $A$, repeats allowed

questions.question: How many ways are there to choose $2$ people from $4$ people, ignoring order?
Two of the four people $A,B,C,D$ are chosen at random, every pair being equally likely. What is the probability that both $A$ and $B$ are chosen?
A club chooses a president, a secretary and a treasurer from $10$ people, each person holding at most one office. Why is the number of outcomes not $\binom{10}{3}$?
options: $\binom{10}{3}$ counts ordered choices, so it overcounts here
The same three people in different offices are different outcomes
Groups of people are never counted by combinations
The positions of the seven people not chosen also matter

questions.question: A committee of $3$ people is chosen from $5$ women and $4$ men, all distinct, and must consist of exactly $2$ women and $1$ man. How many such committees are there?
